title: The weakest pillar
hook: every believer has one pillar to strengthen

segments.voice: Yesterday, the five pillars as one house, and your line: five pillars, one house. Which pillar did you name as your strongest? Hold on to it. Today we turn the question around. Day one thousand one hundred forty-two.

An old house rarely announces which beam is tired. It drops hints. A door that sticks in summer. A hairline crack above a window. A floor that rolls a marble toward one corner. A house isn't mended by admiring the parts that hold. The repair starts the day someone follows the marble. Yesterday asked which of the five pillars stands firmest in your life. Today asks the harder, quieter question: which one is the sticking door? Today, the weakest pillar.
screen: `A DOOR THAT STICKS.` → `FOLLOW THE MARBLE.` → `WHICH ONE STICKS?`

segments.voice: First, the list itself. In that report in Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ names the five: testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His messenger, establishing the prayer, giving zakat, the Hajj, and fasting Ramadan. Five supports for one building. A building with one weak support is still standing, and it is also worth attending to. Second, the scale of the ask. In the last verse of the Qur'an's second surah, in Pickthall's words: "Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope." So the question isn't how to become flawless by Friday. It's what's within reach this week. Third, the size of the step. In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet is asked which deeds are most loved by Allah, and he says the ones done regularly, even if they are small. That turns the whole project around. A weak pillar is rarely mended by one heroic weekend. It's mended by something small that keeps happening. One prayer that used to slip, kept on time. A little set aside each month toward zakat, so the reckoning isn't a shock. For the Hajj, which the Qur'an asks of those who can find a way, the step might be learning its rites, or opening a savings jar. For the testimony, saying it once a day slowly, meaning each word. Fourth, the honest part. Where a pillar has been missed for a long time, prayers or fasts left undone, the schools of law give detailed answers about making them up, and those answers differ. That conversation belongs with a person's own scholar, not with an app. What this day can do is smaller: name the pillar, and choose one step.
screen: `FIVE SUPPORTS FOR ONE BUILDING.` · `NOT BEYOND ITS SCOPE.` · `SMALL, AND REGULAR.` · `DETAILS BELONG WITH A SCHOLAR.`

segments.voice: The practice: plan one step. Settle, and let your breathing slow. Go through the five in your head, one at a time: the testimony, the prayer, zakat, the fast, the Hajj. Notice which one makes you want to skip ahead. That one. Don't scold yourself about it. Just look at it the way a builder looks at a crack: with interest. Now shrink a step until it's almost too easy. Not "pray every prayer from now on". One prayer, one time of day. Decide when, and where you'll be. If you pray, you can ask Allah for help with that one step. If you don't, just hold the plan steady in your mind. The bell holds the time.

The weakest pillar. The one of the five that slips first, and so the one worth strengthening with something small and regular. It closes this block on the pillars: the testimony, the prayer, zakat, the fast, the Hajj. Today's word.

Your line: strengthen one. Today, take the small step you planned, once, and write down when you'll take it again. Tomorrow a new block opens: what a hadith is. Day one thousand one hundred forty-two.

howItsDone: Some Muslims who want to strengthen a pillar start with one regular, small habit, such as one prayer kept on time, and ask a local scholar or imam about making up prayers or fasts that were missed.

fork.setup: you've found your weakest pillar: the prayer slips most days. what's the step the hadith points toward?
options: pray every prayer perfectly, starting tonight.
keep one prayer on time, and keep it up.
wait until you feel ready to do it all.
fork.reveal: the deeds most loved by Allah are the regular ones, even if small. one prayer kept is a beam that holds.
